prompts.text: What's a family story you only found out was unusual when you told somebody else?
Tell me about a relative who could turn a simple errand into an entertaining story.
We're at a gathering and somebody offers to show us an album of very old family pictures. Are you staying for the commentary?
Hearing about the place your parents grew up or the first job an older relative ever had?
The best family stories tend to be about everyday mishaps rather than perfect occasions.
Every family seems to have a relative whose version of events is slightly different from everyone else's.
Have you ever discovered a surprising talent in someone you have known your entire life?
You get to ask an elderly relative three questions about their childhood. Where would you begin?
A family recipe with a handwritten note or an audio recording of somebody telling its story?
Tell me about something you learned about your family over an ordinary meal.
Does your neighbourhood have a story about a place that everybody claims is haunted or mysterious?
I hear an obviously exaggerated tale about a landmark in your town. Would you correct it or add to the legend?
Tell me about an urban legend you believed for longer than you'd like to admit.
Visiting a historical landmark with a guide or hearing a local resident's personal stories about it?
Every town has a building whose history gets more dramatic with each retelling.
A good local legend can make a perfectly ordinary street more memorable.
What's the strangest rumour you heard about your school when you were younger?
We find a plaque describing a completely unexpected event. What would you want to look up afterwards?
A walk through old streets with fascinating histories or an exhibition of unusual local artefacts?
Tell me about a place you thought was ordinary until someone told you its story.
What's one item on your desk or bedside table that says something about your personality?
A messy notebook can tell a more interesting story than a perfectly organised shelf.
We're choosing one object each from a charity shop to decorate a room. What's your selection rule?
An old clock with character or a minimalist lamp that does exactly what it's meant to do?
Tell me about something you bought for a practical reason but ended up feeling attached to.
Some people arrange their books by colour; others would never survive not knowing where anything is.
Have you ever kept the packaging from something because it looked too good to throw away?
I notice a peculiar ornament in your room. Would you rather tell me where it came from or let me guess?
A wall covered in little personal photographs or one carefully chosen piece of artwork?
What's a small object you lost and still occasionally think about?
What's one inexpensive treat you happily spend money on when you've had a demanding week?
The feeling of a small luxury is often more about timing than price.
We each have the equivalent of a modest lunch budget for a surprise treat. What do you spend yours on?
A proper pastry from a bakery or your favourite takeaway eaten somewhere with a view?
Tell me about something you bought for yourself that made an ordinary Tuesday feel special.
Everyone seems to have one purchase they justify with 'It's only a little thing'.
Would you rather save a favourite treat for a special occasion or enjoy it whenever you can?
I suggest a tiny tasting menu at a market stall you've never tried. What would make you give it a go?
A comfortable new notebook or a warm drink served exactly how you like it?
A thoughtful little comfort can be more memorable than an expensive surprise.
Have you ever enjoyed a live performance that surprised you because you didn't expect to like it?
Tell me about a moment on stage that made an entire audience go completely quiet.
An intimate comedy show or a dramatic play in a little theatre?
A performer who makes a mistake and recovers gracefully can make a show even more enjoyable.
We buy tickets to a performance without reading anything about it. Are you excited or suspicious?
The reactions of the people around you can become part of the story of a live show.
Would you rather be seated close enough to see every expression or far enough back to take in the whole stage?
The person next to us starts crying during a scene you found funny. Do you ask what moved them afterwards?
An improvised comedy performance or a carefully rehearsed musical production?
Tell me about a performance you still remember mainly because of the atmosphere in the room.
Is there a sport you'd enjoy watching in person even if you didn't know the rules?
We arrive at a stadium and support opposite teams. What counts as acceptable friendly banter?
Trying to understand cricket together or watching a fast-paced basketball game from the stands?
A crowded room cheering at the same moment can be exciting even when you barely understand the match.
Someone explaining a game's rules patiently makes watching with them much more fun.
Tell me about an unexpected sporting result that you still enjoy talking about.
Have you ever become a fan of an athlete because of their story rather than their performance?
The match turns boring, but the crowd starts singing something funny. Which part of the evening would you remember?
An afternoon watching a friendly local tournament or tickets to a major international event?
Tell me about the first time you went to watch a sport live.
Who's somebody whose calmness you admire, even if you don't know them particularly well?
Tell me about an ordinary person who changed how you approached something.
It's refreshing when somebody can appreciate a role model without pretending they're perfect.
You could have lunch with one living artist, inventor or athlete. What would you hope to learn from them?
Meeting someone who's mastered a craft or someone who's made a real difference in their community?
People sometimes remember a teacher's mannerisms long after forgetting the lesson itself.
Was there somebody at school who made learning feel less intimidating?
I ask you to introduce a person you admire without mentioning their achievements. What quality do you start with?
A conversation with somebody who has decades of experience or somebody your age who's trying something brave?
Tell me about a stranger who taught you something useful in under five minutes.
What's a harmless opinion you hold that nearly everybody around you challenges?
Being able to say 'I hadn't thought of that' is an underrated conversational skill.
We disagree about whether a film deserved its ending. What question would settle whether we understood each other?
A cheerful disagreement about food or one about the best way to spend a weekend?
Tell me about a time a friendly debate introduced you to something you now enjoy.
People reveal their sense of humour in how they handle being wrong about a small thing.
How do you usually react when somebody makes a good point against an opinion you've held for ages?
I confidently claim a simple fact and then learn I'm mistaken. Do you let me recover or bring receipts?
Trying each other's preferred activity or explaining why your own favourite is worth a chance?
You can respect a person's perspective without having to adopt it as your own.
What is it about the start of a new season that makes you want to change something small?
Tell me about a holiday that felt memorable even though you stayed close to home.
We have one free evening during a festive week and everywhere is crowded. What less obvious plan would you suggest?
An evening exploring festive lights or a calm morning visiting a quiet market?
Some places seem to have their own soundtrack whenever a major holiday approaches.
A low-key celebration can feel more personal than an expensive or elaborate one.
Is there a seasonal smell or sound that immediately puts you in a good mood?
You're asked to plan one small activity for a public holiday without spending much. What do you choose?
A yearly tradition you can look forward to or trying something different every holiday season?
Tell me about an ordinary family holiday when an unexpected visitor made the day better.
Do you enjoy having every detail of an outing planned, or is a little uncertainty part of the fun?
Small surprises work best when they're considerate rather than designed to impress.
I say I found a short activity I think you'd like but won't tell you what it is yet. What information would you need before agreeing?
Knowing the destination but not the activity or knowing the activity but not the destination?
Tell me about a time somebody got a small surprise exactly right.
People differ wildly in how much mystery they're comfortable with, even for something as simple as lunch.
What's the most pleasant surprise you've had on an otherwise predictable day?
A café we planned to visit has an unexpected live storytelling session. Would you rearrange the afternoon to listen?
A surprise recommendation from somebody who knows your taste or exploring a place neither of us has researched?
Trusting someone with a plan is easier when they make it clear you can change your mind.
